question: Are the selected learned slot checkpoints numerically valid on real train/validation inputs and at the predictor's planning batch size?
hypothesis: Passing initialization and short synthetic-update checks does not establish validity of selected learned weights; real-input forward/gradient and grouping checks should pass before downstream interpretation.

sources.sections: Floating-point accuracy, batched/slice computations and nonfinite values
sources.consequence: Check actual learned weights and the deployed candidate batch under the existing rtol=1e-4/atol=1e-5, with explicit finite-output/gradient checks. Keep any failure rather than relax tolerance.

sources.sections: Saving/loading for inference; state_dict copy warning; loading across devices
sources.consequence: Load the immutable selected checkpoint in eval mode, bind reviews to its exact digest, and verify no weight or checkpoint mutation.

sources.sections: Appendix G planning configuration, CEM and Hungarian matching; Appendix D/E frozen embeddings
sources.consequence: Exercise full autoregressive candidate rollouts on frozen encoder representations; numerical consistency is distinct from goal-cost quality or planning success. Retain this project's previously frozen B001 settings.

sources.sections: 100 candidates, three-frame history, maximum eight-step horizon
sources.consequence: Use 100 candidates and eight rollout steps for the predictor's batch-grouping test without running or tuning CEM.

sources.sections: selected checkpoint save, load_encoder, extract index and load_world
sources.consequence: Bind predictor checks to actual frozen cache bytes, encoder digest and matching n/seed. Load only executed commands from labels files.

differences: Numerical validation on train/val only, not a new learning or planning experiment. Local B001 uses 100 candidates and horizons 4/6/8, unlike C-JEPA's Push-T settings. No optimizer updates, calibration, precision changes or checkpoint selection. Original L0/L1 final checks remain A003.
contrary_evidence: A finite, numerically consistent model can still bind objects poorly or fail dynamics and planning. Sixteen windows per split and one 100-candidate rollout batch per split are sampled checks, not a proof over all inputs. Slot training and planning use different temporal initialization contexts; cache-fed and independently encoded-history checks remain separate.

scope: actual-input support in existing numerical helper
protocol.models: All selected C001 RGB encoders and O0/O1 predictors in the approved n/seed schedule
protocol.windows: Uniformly sample distinct four-frame flat window indices without replacement with seed,n,split; same selected windows for paired O0/O1. RGB checks use the first three frames. Predictor checks use four cached states and three executed commands /3.
protocol.checks: CPU/GPU eval outputs and every trainable parameter gradient; GPU repeat, reversal and separate-item outputs. RGB includes decoder reconstruction/masks. Predictor checks unmasked inference plus the fixed two-example history masks for O1. Reject nonfinite values explicitly.
protocol.planning_batch: For each split, independently encode the first selected three-frame history, replicate to 100 candidates, append eight norm-capped Gaussian actions (std2) to the two executed history commands, then compare eight-step GPU predictor rollouts batched, repeated, reversed and in batches of two. No CEM or score optimization; no future observations in the rollout input.
protocol.lineage: Require reviewed selected checkpoint; predictors also require a passing C004 encoder review, matching encoder/cache/seed/n and actual cache bytes. Hash train/val frames, actions container and metadata; record sampled indices. Verify learned state and source checkpoint unchanged after checks.
verification: fixed split-specific sampling with valid history/future indices
tampered cache or mismatched n/seed rejected before GPU work

success: Every declared check passes at the unchanged tolerance and weights/checkpoint are unchanged. A hash-bound C004 review then supplies the inference artifact review for cache extraction, binding, learned planning or probes as applicable.
stop: Any missing gradient, nonfinite value, state mutation or numerical mismatch blocks downstream interpretation pending substantive review. Preserve failed measurements. No retry with altered precision, samples or tolerance without a new preregistration. No new full GPU work alongside original trainers.

resources.scope: per selected checkpoint, within the shared validation reserve and 48-hour allowance
resources.training_device: none; CPU reference derivatives and dedicated GPU inference only
